answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network isolates suspected clusters onto a topological cut or trust island, where game-theoretic multi-agent auditing inspects flow bottlenecks. A challenger stakes capital to summon peer auditors; if cross-cluster cut verifications expose fake identities, cartel deposits face stake slashing. Attacking costs scale with superlinear attacker cost because expanding coordinated nodes requires bonded collateral that faces a gale of cascading penalties, ensuring even a nimble sparrow cannot mask synthetic collusion.
